plan.title: AD treated vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000 genes x 12 samples of raw Salmon gene-level counts from human skin, 6 treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) vs 6 control, single batch, unpaired, with sample_01 flagged at ~4x below median library size. The plan follows the grounded full_plan procedure: (1) sample-structure QC with blind vst, PCA, and distance heatmap, where sample_01 is kept, inspected, and reported per R-0008 — the size factors down-weight a low-depth sample, so removal is a judgment requiring stated evidence, not a default; (2) a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) followed by DESeq2 with median-of-ratios size factors, Wald test, apeglm-shrunken LFC, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, answering 'which genes change'; (3) an edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same counts as the second method, with the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence gene set (6 replicates per group is the low end of agreement between the two tools); (4) fgsea preranked GSEA of all tested genes ranked by the Wald statistic (the stated choice in the disputed rank-metric rule) against the staged MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1 collection, whose HGNC-symbol space matches the symbol-keyed counts — no identifier remap is needed and the unmapped share of each set is reported, answering 'which hallmark pathways change'; (5) a consolidated report carrying the MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, both effect columns, leading-edge genes per significant set, the sample_01 verdict with its stated reason, and the full reproducibility record. Counts are gene-level only (no transcript quant files), so the tximport length-offset rule is recorded as not applicable rather than silently ignored.
